newsitem.title: UK: London gold firmer after bounce, upside limited.
newsitem.headline: London gold firmer after bounce, upside limited.

text.p: The price of gold firmed on Friday in what dealers said was a temporary correction in a sliding market.

Bullion was fixed at $358.55 an ounce, compared to $356.50 on Thursday afternoon and more than $3 up from the London close. "The market is finally showing a spark of life. If we're able to close around $360 today, it will augur well for gold next week," one dealer said.
Dealers attributed gold's bounce, from Thursday's fresh 3-1/4 year lows below $354 an ounce, to overnight shortcovering and Japanese buying.

Prices ticked higher in New York late on Thursday, as investment funds covered some of their short positions. This was followed by buying by Japanese traders in reaction to a falling dollar/yen and a sharp drop in the Tokyo stock market.
The price was also boosted by the absence of Australian producer selling in overnight Asian markets, a dealer said.
"That was the first time in a long time," he added.
Prices later flattened out in European trading, but gold may yet move up to nearby $360 resistance, dealers and analysts said, where resistance was expected to be stiff.
Above that level, prices could surge to $365 next week in the absence of significant technical resistance.
But the bounce, which follows a very steep tumble since the start of the year, is expected to be sold down before long.
"Even though prices are higher, gold isn't looking strong. There's no reason for investment funds to take their ample profits yet," one dealer said.
Eventually gold is headed towards the important $345-$343 support area, with the psychological $350 level also expected to provide a bit of support, several analysts said.

"This market needs to go down to $342, which seems like a nice place to bottom out going back to 1993," a trader said, referring to a 1993 key low. Silver prices were indicated five cents firmer at $4.75/$4.77, after ticking up with gold.
Silver's next upside target was $4.80-$4.82, although it has already met resistance around $4.77, dealers said.
Platinum, which has been tailing gold, was indicated $2.25 fimrer at $462.25/$363.25.
Palladium was also up slightly from Thursday's closing levels, at $122.00/$123.00. It was trading at four-month highs amid concerns over delays in supplies from key producer Russia.
